## Popular childhood cereal gets an unexpected protein makeover
For decades, General Mills’ colorful, fruit-flavored Trix cereal has been a childhood breakfast favorite, thanks in part to its mischievous rabbit mascot.

Now, the nostalgic cereal is getting a protein-packed makeover aimed at a new audience: adults increasingly focused on fitness, nutrition and healthier eating habits.

The maker of Cheerios, Lucky Charms and Cinnamon Toast Crunch has teamed up with sports nutrition brand GHOST to introduce a protein-enhanced version of Trix containing 17 grams of protein per serving.
## General Mills brings protein-maxxing to Trix
The new GHOST Protein Cereal x Trix retains the familiar fruity flavor associated with the original cereal while offering significantly more protein.

According to GHOST, each serving contains 17 grams of protein, is a good source of calcium and uses colors from natural sources. The cereal is being marketed as an option for breakfast, post-workout meals and snacking.

**More Retail:**
The product reflects the growing popularity of protein-maxxing, a trend that has encouraged food companies to introduce higher-protein versions of everything from snacks and beverages to breakfast staples.

General Mills has already been experimenting with the approach.

In February 2026, the company announced GHOST Protein Cereal versions of Cinnamon Toast Crunch and Lucky Charms, each offering 17 grams of protein per serving.
## General Mills is changing more than its cereal recipes
The company is investing in product development, packaging and consumer value to restore growth. The protein-enhanced Trix cereal is one example of how it hopes to do that.

But at nearly $10 per box through GHOST’s online store, the product also highlights another challenge for traditional cereal makers: convincing cost-conscious consumers that a familiar breakfast staple is worth paying more for because of the nutritional updates.

Trix has already made the jump from the breakfast aisle to the shaker through Ghost’s [authentic Whey Protein collaboration](https://www.stack3d.com/2026/03/trix-ghost-whey-protein-powder/), although that version delivers the taste without cereal pieces. The lifestyle brand is now giving the General Mills favorite a place in the bowl with almost as much protein. Ghost has unveiled a Trix flavor of its Protein Cereal already available in Lucky Charms and Cinnamon Toast Crunch, and this one comes with the familiar colorful puffs.
The authentic collaboration brings Trix’s fruity flavor to a cereal built primarily around milk concentrate, sodium caseinate, and soy isolate, with whey concentrate also contributing for a total of 17g of protein per serving. GHOST protein cereals contain 17g of protein per serving from a blend of milk protein concentrate, soy protein isolate and whey protein concentrate. The Trix version also contains 160 calories, 7g fat and 11g of carbohydrates.
